newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada court rejects bid to halt Voisey's Bay work. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canada court rejects bid to halt Voisey's Bay work. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]

text.p: The Supreme Court of Newfoundland on Friday dismissed a native group's bid to stop two construction projects at Inco Ltd's massive Voisey's Bay nickel project.
The Labrador Inuit Association had asked the court to block construction of an airstrip and road for the project in a remote area of Labrador.
The Inuit group argued that the projects are production work and should not be approved by the Newfoundland government until a broader environmental review of Voisey's Bay is completed.
Toronto-based Inco maintained the airstrip and road are needed to support ongoing exploration of the site.
"The works are necessary to support the ongoing exploratory activity," Justice Raymond Halley (corrects from James Halley) said in a written decision released on Friday.
"The application of the Inuit is dismissed and the Inuit shall pay costs to the province and the company," Halley said.

Voisey's Bay, one of the world's biggest nickel-copper-cobalt deposits, is slated to start producing concentrate in late 1999 and refined nickel by late 2000. Annual output is forecast at 270 million pounds of nickel when the mine reaches full production in 2001.
Analysts had said Voisey's Bay could have been delayed another year if the Newfoundland court had ruled in favor of the Inuit group.
